Scope and effective date (last updated August 31, 2026): This Agreement is between you and the developer and provider of FolderSpan ("we" or "us") and applies to FolderSpan's base features on Android, iOS, desktop, and the web. By selecting agree, installing, or continuing to use FolderSpan, you acknowledge this Agreement and the Privacy Policy. If you do not agree, stop using the software.

Permissions and elevated access: To perform actions you choose, FolderSpan may request file or media access, local-network access, notifications, background operation, battery-optimization exemptions, and launch-at-boot or sign-in capabilities. Android all-files access, Root, or Shizuku can greatly expand accessible data and should be enabled only when necessary and understood. You may revoke permissions in system or app settings, but affected features may stop working.

Instructions and automation: Copy, move, rename, delete, edit, upload, download, synchronization, sharing, and MCP automation actions run from your immediate instructions, saved rules, or authorized Tokens and may directly change data on this device, trusted devices, or remote storage. Before enabling schedules, background services, automatic sharing or receiving, or automation interfaces, verify paths, scope, conflict policies, and access rights.

Third-party and self-hosted services: When you connect FTP, SFTP, SMB, WebDAV, S3, WebRTC signaling/STUN/TURN services or open an external website, you interact directly with the relevant service provider or device and are subject to its terms, privacy practices, availability, and fees. We do not control or guarantee the servers, network routes, recipients, security, or continued availability you select.

Acceptable use: You must not use FolderSpan to access devices, accounts, directories, or networks without authorization; bypass controls; attack or disrupt systems; distribute malware or unlawful content; infringe privacy, intellectual-property, or other rights; or provide sharing links, MCP Tokens, or connection credentials to unauthorized persons.

Sharing and connection security: Link sharing, browser uploads, device connections, WebRTC, and MCP can make selected content or capabilities reachable by others on a network. Use trusted networks, set passwords and least-privilege scopes where appropriate, verify device names and TLS certificate fingerprints, and promptly disable or rotate exposed links, tickets, and Tokens. A self-signed certificate warning does not establish trust; you decide whether to connect.

Data and backups: File operations may be irreversible, and cross-device or remote operations may be affected by outages, permission changes, server behavior, disk failures, or incompatibilities. Back up important data and verify results before bulk move, overwrite, delete, synchronize, or writable sharing operations. FolderSpan history, caches, recovery files, and task status are not a substitute for backups.

Service changes: Features differ by platform, operating-system version, and protocol support, and laboratory features may be unstable. We may fix, change, suspend, or discontinue features for security, compatibility, legal, or product reasons and may update this Agreement. Material changes will be communicated through the app, release channels, or official website where appropriate.

Intellectual property: The FolderSpan name, interface, documentation, and software works other than open-source components are protected by applicable law. You receive a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable license to use the software under this Agreement. Third-party open-source components remain governed by their respective licenses, available through the app's open-source notices.

Responsibility and disclaimers: To the extent permitted by law, FolderSpan is provided as is without a promise of uninterrupted, error-free operation or compatibility with every file system, device, or remote service. Responsibility for disclosure, credential exposure, data loss, or charges caused by your configuration, unauthorized actions, untrusted recipients, or third-party services rests with the responsible party. Nothing here excludes liability that cannot lawfully be excluded.

Stopping use and cleanup: You may stop using FolderSpan, disable network services, and delete connections and records at any time. Use Clear app data, clear browser site data, or uninstall to remove local data. Copies already delivered to other devices, sharing recipients, or remote services are not automatically removed by local cleanup and must be handled with the relevant recipient or provider.

Minors: Users below the legal age in their location should use FolderSpan only after a guardian has reviewed and accepted these terms. Guardians should help minors avoid exposing files, device addresses, links, credentials, or other personal information. Personal information of children under 14 must be decided and managed by their guardian where Chinese law applies.

Law and contact: Mandatory consumer, network-security, data, and intellectual-property laws in your location continue to apply. Please first raise disputes through the FolderSpan website at https://www.folderspan.com or the developer contact published by your software distribution channel. If unresolved, either party may pursue remedies before a competent authority under applicable law.

Scope and controller (last updated August 31, 2026): This Policy explains how FolderSpan's base features process information on this device, devices you choose, and network services you configure. The controller is the developer and provider of FolderSpan. Contact channels are https://www.folderspan.com and the developer contact published by your software distribution channel.

Processing principles: FolderSpan defaults to on-device processing and uses data within the functionally necessary, minimum scope directed by you. Base features can operate without centrally uploading local files to a FolderSpan-operated server. Processing is generally necessary to perform software functions you request, based on your consent, or necessary for security and legal compliance.

Local files and content: When you browse, search, preview, analyze, edit, copy, move, rename, delete, share, or transfer files, FolderSpan processes the selected directory and file names, paths, types, sizes, timestamps, permissions, thumbnails, and necessary content. The editor may create local backup or recovery data. This data stays in your device or browser storage by default.

Device discovery, connections, and messages: LAN scans and device connections process device identifiers, names and types, IP addresses, ports, connection methods, first and latest connection times, role permissions, certificates, and fingerprints. Messages, files, directory information, and transfer status you send go to the selected peer. Message bodies and conversation state may be stored in the local databases of both devices.

Link sharing and receiving: When you create a sharing link or run a sharing service, your device serves selected files, directories, names, path metadata, access rules, password state, temporary tickets, and transfer status. A recipient with a valid link, ticket, or password can download within the granted scope. If you enable browser uploads or writing, recipients can also submit or change content at authorized locations.

Network locations and credentials: To connect to FTP, SFTP, SMB, WebDAV, or S3, FolderSpan stores and uses the name, protocol, server address, username, password, private key, Tokens, custom headers, bucket, region, and related settings, and sends required paths, file content, and request metadata to the service you chose. Passwords and extended credentials are stored locally in encrypted form and decrypted locally when used.

WebRTC: Cross-device WebRTC processes room identifiers, signaling, STUN and TURN addresses and credentials, peer devices, connection candidates, and related network information. Signaling data goes to the signaling service you choose. If direct connection fails, a TURN service may relay file or message traffic. Room settings and credentials are stored locally in encrypted form.

Clipboard, external open, and imports: FolderSpan reads relevant clipboard text, URLs, file references, or content granted by another app only when you invoke paste, open, or share-import actions, and uses it to preview, copy, or download. When you visit a pasted URL, the corresponding website or server receives ordinary request information such as your IP address and request headers.

MCP automation: The MCP HTTP service is off by default and listens only on this device unless you separately permit LAN access. FolderSpan locally stores its port, switches, Token names, secret hashes, scopes, creation and update times, and last-used times. A client holding a full Token can read or change bookmarks, favorites, recents, tasks, devices, networks, and files within its scopes. Full secrets appear only on creation or rotation.

Logs and crash information: Automatic log capture is off by default. When enabled, FolderSpan caches up to approximately 2 MiB of runtime logs locally, potentially including times, errors, stack traces, file paths, device names, server addresses, and operation status. Crash summaries may also be retained locally. Base logging does not send this data automatically; it leaves the device only when you explicitly copy, export, or submit it.

System permissions: File or media access supports file management; local-network and network-state access supports discovery, connections, sharing, and MCP; notifications support transfer, request, and error alerts; foreground services, wake locks, battery exemptions, alarms, and startup support background tasks you enable; Root or Shizuku supports explicitly selected elevated file access. Your operating system manages these permissions, and you can revoke them.

Sharing, processors, and third parties: The current base features do not integrate advertising or behavioral-analytics SDKs, and we do not sell personal information. Data is provided to a device, recipient, server, or external app you select only when you choose sharing, connecting, downloading, uploading, WebRTC relaying, external links, or automation. Open-source libraries support file, network, database, image, and notification functions locally and do not by themselves receive your data.

International transfers: We do not centrally arrange international transfers of files for base features. If you configure a foreign server, object store, signaling/STUN/TURN service, or share with a recipient abroad, related data may travel internationally at your direction. Before doing so, understand the recipient, purpose, data categories, safeguards, and rights process, and ensure the transfer complies with applicable law.

Retention and security: Local records generally remain until you delete an item, clear app data or browser site data, or uninstall. Some records such as recents have count limits, while caches and temporary tickets may expire sooner. FolderSpan uses controls including encrypted credentials, Token hashing, TLS, self-signed certificate fingerprints, permission scopes, and access checks, but no device, LAN, or internet transfer can be absolutely secure.

Your choices and rights: In FolderSpan you can view, correct, or delete devices, messages, network locations, WebRTC rooms, bookmarks, favorites, recents, tasks, and sharing settings; disable logs, MCP, sharing, background operation, and notifications; revoke system permissions; and use Clear app data or uninstall to erase local data. Contact the relevant recipient for data already delivered to a third party. Submit other access, copy, correction, deletion, or explanation requests through the official contact channels.

Children's information: FolderSpan is not designed to collect children's information. Minors should use it under guardian supervision. Where Chinese law applies, guardian consent is required before processing personal information of a child under 14. A guardian who believes inappropriate information was processed may use the official contact channels to request an explanation or deletion.

Policy updates and contact: If features, data categories, recipients, or legal requirements materially change, we will update this Policy and provide notice through the app, release channel, or official website, and obtain renewed consent when required. Questions, complaints, or rights requests may be sent through https://www.folderspan.com or the developer contact published by your software distribution channel.

Content rights and responsibility: You must have the right to access, edit, share, copy, move, delete, upload, or automate the files, messages, and settings involved and remain responsible for their legality, accuracy, and backup. Do not process state secrets, work secrets, or data that applicable law prohibits from being handled through the relevant device, network, or third-party service.
